text:
rachel_garcia: Hi team — I moved from OR to WA last month and need to switch my PCP and confirm my coverage for an upcoming specialist visit. My appointment is 2025-05-07. How do I update my PCP and will my out-of-state claims be covered during the transition?

tiffany_benefits: Congrats on the move! Quick steps: Workday > Benefits > Provider Directory to search in-network WA PCPs > Update Primary Care Provider. If the dropdown doesn't show WA options, reply here and we'll open a case.

rachel_garcia: Dropdown only shows OR providers still. I updated home address in Workday last week — does that need to propagate?

paul_hr: Address change can take 24-48 hours to sync to carrier. If it's past that window we can manually push a sync. When did you change it?

rachel_garcia: Changed on 2025-04-20. It's been 10 days.

tiffany_benefits: Thanks — we'll trigger a carrier sync. Meanwhile, for your 2025-05-07 specialist appt: is the specialist in-network in WA? If not, we can request a one-time out-of-network exception or prior authorization depending on specialty.

rachel_garcia: It's a neurology consult at Seattle Neuro Clinic — looks like out-of-network in the carrier portal. Can benefits request an exception?

paul_hr: Carriers sometimes approve continuity-of-care exceptions for moves or urgent consults. We'll need: provider name, NPI (if available), appointment date, and a short medical necessity note from your referring PCP. Upload those to benefits and we'll submit an exception request.

rachel_garcia: I don't have an NPI handy. I can get the referral note from my OR PCP. How fast do carriers respond to exception requests?

tiffany_benefits: Timeline varies: routine auths ~3-7 business days, expedited reviews available for urgent cases. If you need coverage confirmation before the appointment, flag it as expedited and include a reason (e.g., time-sensitive diagnostic). We'll do that when we submit.

carrier-bot: Reminder: If address sync completes before appointment, you must select an in-network WA specialist for standard in-network benefits to apply. Exception approvals do not retroactively convert claims to in-network rates unless specified.

rachel_garcia: Understood. I'll upload the referral note and provider contact details now. If exception denied, what's the fallback for minimizing OON costs?

paul_hr: Fallbacks: request a negotiated single-case agreement with the provider (we can ask carrier to negotiate rates), or reschedule with an in-network WA specialist. Also save itemized bills and superbills — we can help with appeals for partial reimbursement if denial happens.

tiffany_benefits: Upload to Workday > Benefits > Documents > Add Document and include filename like "rachel_neuro_referral_050125.pdf". If upload fails, email benefits@redwood.com with subject "State move PCP sync - rachel_garcia".

rachel_garcia: Uploaded referral and provider info. Thanks — appreciate the help!

people-ops-bot: Intake ticket created: #HR-85390. Benefits will update you in 1 business day about carrier sync and exception submission.
